question: A thief running at a speed of 8 km/h is chased by a policeman whose speed is 10 km/h. If the thief is 100 m ahead of the policeman, then the time required for the policeman to catch the thief will be:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed of policeman = 10 − 8 = 2 km/h

Distance gap to close = 100 m = 0.1 km

Time required = Distance ÷ Relative speed = 0.1 ÷ 2 = 1/20 hours

Time in minutes = 1/20 × 60 = 3 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 3 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of the policeman (Sₚ) = 10 km/h

Speed of the thief (Sₜ) = 8 km/h

Initial distance ahead (D) = 100 m = 0.1 km

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed = Sₚ − Sₜ (Since they move in the same direction)

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e608d9911945b0b381ea958572edfa19dc2c6160b6bab924db96c7070f4db41a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 10 − 8 = 2 km/h

⇒ Time required to catch the thief = 0.1 km ÷ 2 km/h = 0.05 hours

⇒ To convert hours into minutes, multiply by 60:

⇒ Time required = 0.05 × 60 = 3 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 3 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two bodies move in the same direction at speeds S₁ and S₂ (where S₁ > S₂), their relative speed is S₁ − S₂.

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two bodies move towards each other at speeds S₁ and S₂, their relative speed is S₁ + S₂.

Speed Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply the speed by 5 ÷ 18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18 ÷ 5.
